name: discrawl-54eb70cf-blind30-ots
instr:
# discrawl: thirty silent behaviour changes to find without a test suite

This is a command-line tool that pulls a chat server's history into a local database, answers questions about it, hands copies of that history to other people and takes copies in from them. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits. Nothing about the chat service changed and nothing about my saved preferences changed, yet the same things I have done for months now come back wrong, and in several places an operation that used to succeed stops with a complaint instead. What follows is everything I have been able to pin down from using the tool, in the order I ran into it.

Setting the tool up and signing in is where I first noticed it. Signing in against the hosted endpoint and saving the session secret it hands back files that secret under an empty account label, and nothing can be read back afterwards under that empty label. A secret saved with surrounding whitespace comes back with the whitespace still attached instead of the trimmed text, and an entry that holds nothing but spaces is handed out as a usable credential rather than refused for being empty. With no environment variable set, asking for the bot's login secret out of the operating system's credential vault fails as though the entry were empty even though the entry plainly holds a value, and asking for the hosted endpoint's secret fails the same way once my preferences point at a service and account name of my own choosing. V
